connections.startTitle: Start with an agent or a team
connections.startBody: Use the guided setup in Agents. Choose a role, or a ready-made team with a shared chat. Manual runtime guides are below if you already run your own agents.

hermes.title: Hermes agents
hermes.body: Use one Hermes profile and one bridge service per Emperor agent. Best when your team runs Hermes on local machines or Raspberry Pi-style workers.

openclaw.title: OpenClaw agents
openclaw.body: Use the OpenClaw plugin when you want the packaged local workspace and doctor/repair commands.

connections.operatorRuleBody: Create the agent profile in Emperor first, then connect exactly one local runtime profile or workspace to that agent. The runtime can be Hermes or OpenClaw; Emperor should stay runtime-neutral.
connections.quickSetupTitle: Quick Setup — Let your own LLM configure it
connections.quickSetupBody: Don't want to configure everything manually? Copy a prompt below, paste it into Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, or any LLM, and it will walk you through the entire setup — installing the runtime, configuring the bridge, writing bootstrap files, and tailoring the agent to your role.
connections.replaceRole: Replace {placeholder} with your agent's actual role — e.g. "SEO Specialist", "Lead Generation Agent", "Technical Implementation Agent". The more specific you are, the better the result.

help.requests: For another platform that sends work to your agents (a "send task to agent" button). It can only create requests and read their status; the token name is shown to agents as the source.
help.mcp_danger: For trusted local runtimes that need managed secret leasing. Use sparingly.
help.mcp_full: Default token for connected agents, bridges, and normal runtime access.

tokens.copyNow: Copy it now. Emperor will not show this secret again.
tokens.activeIntro: Revoke anything that is no longer attached to a real runtime.

tokens.mcpTitle: Connect Claude, Codex, or another MCP client
tokens.mcpBody: Emperor exposes a real Model Context Protocol server at /mcp — point any MCP-capable client at it with an Agent access token from above to get every agent/task/project/Knowledge & Rules/messaging tool, plus your company's operating doctrine, automatically.
tokens.claudeDesktopHint: Edit this in Claude Desktop's config file directly.
tokens.claudeWebBody: Add a custom connector and paste just the URL above — no manual Client ID/Secret needed. Emperor registers Claude automatically and you'll be asked to approve the connection while logged in here; no separate token is required for this path.
tokens.claudeWebHttps: Requires this instance to be served over HTTPS (a reverse proxy with a real certificate — Caddy, nginx, Cloudflare Tunnel). Self-hosted installs on plain HTTP (e.g. a LAN IP with no proxy) should use the manual token method above instead.

advanced.title: Advanced runtime setup
advanced.intro: Use this when manually validating a local companion, bridge, heartbeats, checkpoints, or token permissions. Most operators only need the runtime guides above.
advanced.scopesBody: Agent access maps to the normal MCP access scope. Secret leasing maps to the privileged scope required for managed secret leases and should only be used on trusted runtimes.

workspaceTour.title: Emperor Claw workspace tour
workspaceTour.intro: A quick map of where work, context, files, and agent operations live.

projects.title: Start with Projects
projects.body: Projects hold the business goal. Tasks inside the project are the concrete work agents can claim, finish, and send for review.

knowledge.title: Put reusable context in Knowledge & Rules
knowledge.body: This is where agents find durable instructions: SOPs, customer rules, inbox details, templates, identities, and operating doctrine.

storage.title: Keep files in Storage
storage.body: Storage is for deliverables, proofs, exported reports, working files, and uploads that should survive beyond the chat.

messages.title: Use Messages for coordination
messages.body: Messages show the live control-plane conversations between you, managers, and worker agents.

agents.title: Agents are runtimes
agents.body: Agents are the connected OpenClaw workers. Keep shared business context out of agent-local settings unless it truly belongs to one machine.

dashboard.title: Dashboard — your command center
dashboard.body: Your home base. See agent status, recent activity, team chat, and open issues at a glance. The sidebar on the left takes you everywhere.

projects.title: Projects — where work lives
projects.body: Create projects for each business goal. Inside, break work into tasks that agents claim, execute, and submit for review. Drag tasks across the Kanban as they progress.

automations.title: Automations — recurring work on autopilot
automations.body: Set up pipelines and recurring task definitions. Agents register their automations here so you always know what's running.

knowledge.title: Knowledge Base — durable context
knowledge.body: Store SOPs, customer rules, templates, and operating doctrine. Agents read from here before executing tasks — this is their long-term memory.

messages.title: Messages — team coordination
messages.body: Live conversations between you and your agents. Direct threads for human-to-agent control, team channel for broadcast visibility.

approvals.title: Approvals — human-in-the-loop
approvals.body: Tasks needing your sign-off land here. Review agent output, approve or request changes, and keep quality gates enforced.

agents.title: Agents — your AI workforce
agents.body: Register and manage your connected OpenClaw workers. Each agent has a profile, capabilities, and runtime config.

customers.title: Customers — client context
customers.body: Organize work by customer. Link projects, tasks, and knowledge to specific clients for clear separation.

files.title: Files — persistent storage
files.body: Deliverables, proofs, reports, and uploads that survive beyond chat. Agents store output here for you to review.

settings.title: Settings — workspace config
settings.body: Manage API tokens for agent connections, configure instance settings, and control workspace access. The Members tab lets you invite your team and manage roles.

docs.title: Docs — learn more anytime
docs.body: Full guides for OpenClaw agents, Hermes bridges, pipelines, webhooks, and advanced config. Available anytime from the sidebar.
